mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat from intestinal cells into chylomicrons and then lymph was most worthwhile: the planned pictures and prose connect an unfamiliar particle name to its role in transport.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate glucose and amino-acid crossings felt repetitive. Both planned pictures show entry into a capillary but leave the crossing mechanisms unspecified.

surprise.text: I did not expect the explanation to say that intestinal cells rebuild fat before packaging it into chylomicrons.

arbitrary.text: Combining glucose and amino acids already in villus blood felt somewhat artificial, although the resulting shared route toward the liver had a clear purpose. The term “portal” was not explicitly explained.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the absorbed nutrients are used, though the offered compatible combinations made this chapter's decisions fairly straightforward.
